claims.statement: Sherman Thurston seconded Tom Allen in his fight with Jem Mace in 1870.
Tom Allen trained for the Mace fight in St. Louis under Jack Goulding and Joe Coburn.
Before the fight, Mike McCoole bet Tom Allen $500 more that he would win, and lent Allen $200 to cover the bet because Allen had only $300.
Referee Eph Holland of Boston was said to have been fixed to give Goss the decision.
Fred Watkins, Allen's backer, was said to have lost $1,000 to referee Eph Holland at the Goss fight.
Fred Watkins, Allen's backer, lost $1,000 to referee Eph Holland, who took it to bet on Joe Goss.
After the Mace fight, Tom Allen received a $1,000 forfeit from Mike McCoole.
Tom Allen was seen drunk a few days before the Mace fight and entered the ring heavier than his usual 175 pounds (figure garbled).
Tom Allen trained for the Mace fight at the Wash Home (town name unreadable).
Tom Allen got half the excursion money from the Mace fight and had to split it with his backers Billy Carroll and John Franklin.
That night Tom Allen played the piano with both hands, which he could not have done with a broken arm.
Tom Allen seconded George Seddons (with Patsey Curtin) against John Lafferty on Carroll Island, Illinois, on 25 January 1870, and took charge of Seddons before the fight.
Tom Allen seconded George Carey (with Patsey Curtin) against James C. Gallagher on Carroll Island, Illinois, on 25 January 1870.
Tom Allen threw up the sponge for George Carey, who was beaten by James C. Gallagher, on Carroll Island in 18 minutes.
Tom Allen's friends in St. Louis said he was the strongest and as active and scientific as Mace, and would bet their bottom dollar that he would beat him.
Mace said an item in the St. Louis Evening Dispatch had evidently been inserted at Tom Allen's request as an advertisement of his own pretensions.
Tom Allen complained that Mace had not called on him.
Tom Allen went into training at the Wash House under Jack Gelding for his fight with Jem Mace near New Orleans.
Joe Coburn, Mike McCoole and Billy Carroll visited Tom Allen at his training quarters at the Wash House on Tuesday, 19 April 1870, a reunion of old ring rivals.
A belt made by Jaccard was to be presented to Tom Allen at his benefit.
Jack Looney had publicly predicted, about a week before the fight, that Allen would be defeated because he was not in proper condition.
Joe Coburn is reported to be Tom Allen's second in the approaching fight with Mace on 10 May 1870.
Joe Coburn and Thurston seconded Tom Allen against Jem Mace.
Tom Allen weighed 175 pounds on the day of the Mace fight.
Joe Coburn seconded Tom Allen in the fight with Jem Mace.
Jack Looney said the Mace fight was a sham, a put-up job.
Billy Carroll accepted John C. Heenan's proposal of Rufus Hunt as referee.
Billy Carroll spoke to the crowd on Tom Allen's behalf, saying Allen had never had a fair show.
Joe Coburn and Sherman Thurston seconded Tom Allen in his fight with Mace.
Tom Allen was said not to have trained down: his fighting weight was 175 pounds but he had not got below 190.
Mrs. Allen took with her the belt that Allen's St. Louis friends had presented to him.
A belt proposed for Allen some time ago was to be presented to him at the entertainment.
Dr. Morse said that a $1,000 premium at an agricultural fair might get Tom Allen or Mike McCoole for a prize fight.
Tom Allen backed Punch Morris in the $100 fight with Steve O'Donnell, and Jack Leoney backed O'Donnell.
Punch Morris and Owen Meeker, quartered at the Wash Home, were to be trained by the trainer of Tom Allen.
Allen eased his training for a few days after a report that Gallagher was sick.
Allen stopped training and was rather full in flesh after hearing that Gallagher was sick.
Betting on the fight was two to one, with few willing to back Gallagher.
Tom Allen bet $1,000 to $600 that he could whip the winner of the Owen Meekin and James C. Gallagher match.
Mace and B. Aaron were to be the seconds of Tom Allen for the fight with Gallagher.
Tom Allen said he was never better and weighed 180 pounds when stripped (printed as 180 wounds).
Barney Aaron and George Collins seconded Allen.
Allen gave $50 of the $100 subscribed for Gallagher after the fight.
The garbled text seems to name Tom Allen at the ring where Mace was sitting, but the reading is uncertain (printed as 'Tom Ailes').
Tom Allen was to train Jem Mace four miles from St. Louis and back him for a sum printed as 200 against Ned O'Baldwin.
Tom Allen seconded Jem Mace in Mace's drawn fight with Joe Coburn at Bay St. Louis on November 30, 1871.
Tom Allen of St. Louis was named as one of Jem Mace's seconds for the Mace-Coburn fight near New Orleans.
Tom Allen seconded Jem Mace in the Mace-Coburn fight near New Orleans.
Tom Allen was among the prize-ring notables present at the Mace-Coburn fight.
Tom Allen was one of Jem Mace's seconds in the Mace-Coburn fight at Montgomery Station, Mississippi.
Tom Allen was among the notables of the prize ring present at the Mace-Coburn fight.
Tom Allen said he claimed a foul for Mace at the fight, but the referee would not listen.
A man pulled a revolver on Tom Allen at the Mace-Coburn fight and told him to shut up (printed as puiled a rmevoiver).
Tom Allen was extremely excited on August 21, 1872, waiting near the telegraph office for news of the reported Mace and O'Baldwin fight.
Tom Allen said that O'Baldwin was too much for Mace in the reported fight.
